issues.title: Wrong RFC 9460 section cited for no-default-alpn
issues.author: ekinnear
issues.body: Section 3.1 (Wire Format) says the empty value follows the pattern of "no-default-alpn", "defined in Section 7.1.2 of RFC 9460". The rule that the "no-default-alpn" value MUST be empty is in Section 7.1.1 (Representation). Section 7.1.2 (Use) covers how clients build the ALPN set.

issues.title: Latency benefit depends on address hints, which RFC 9460 §7.3 discourages
issues.author: ekinnear
issues.body:
The flag lets a client reuse the SVCB/HTTPS record, including its `ipv4hint` and `ipv6hint`, after a network change. It doesn't cover the A/AAAA records for the TargetName. Without hints, a client that moves networks still has to resolve A/AAAA on the new network before it can connect, so the flag only allows it to avoid waiting for the HTTPS query.

RFC 9460 §7.3 says hints SHOULD NOT be included if most clients use compliant recursive resolvers, and that operators SHOULD NOT include them when the TargetName is "." "because they are unlikely to convey any performance benefit". Operators following that guidance would get little from this flag. The draft's own example in §3.2 has TargetName "." and no hints:

    example.com. 300 IN HTTPS 1 . alpn=h2,h3 globally-relevant

Proposal:

- Say explicitly that the flag covers only the record that carries it, not A/AAAA records for the TargetName.
- Explain that the latency benefit comes from address hints, that §7.3's reason for leaving them out doesn't apply to flagged records, and recommend that operators setting the flag include hints that are valid on all networks.
- Add hints to the example.

An alternative would be for the flag to also cover A/AAAA at the TargetName when it is "." (same owner name and zone).

pulls.title: Adjust text forbidding resolver modification
pulls.author: bemasc
pulls.body: The present text could be read to imply that this is a special restriction for this flag (as opposed to a rule about SvcParams or RDATA generally).  It could also be read to suggest that resolvers are permitted to modify DNS records in some cases.  (Even when performing filtering, _modification_ of records is not appropriate or permitted.)

pulls.title: Fix no-default-alpn section reference
pulls.author: ekinnear
pulls.body:
The empty-value rule for "no-default-alpn" is in Section 7.1.1 of RFC 9460, not 7.1.2. This also switches to the `{{Section X of RFCY}}` form used elsewhere in the draft, so the reference links to the section.

Closes #2

pulls.title: Add guidance on address hints
pulls.author: ekinnear
pulls.body:
- Client Behavior: state that the flag covers only the record that carries it, not A/AAAA records for the TargetName.
- Server Behavior: explain that the latency benefit after a network change comes from address hints, note that the RFC 9460 §7.3 reason for omitting hints doesn't apply to flagged records, and recommend (SHOULD) that operators setting the flag include hints that are valid on all networks.
- Presentation Format: add hints to the example.

Closes #3
